newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL SHARES SURGE 5.16 PCT AS TELEBRAS SOARS.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL SHARES SURGE 5.16 PCT AS TELEBRAS SOARS.

text.p: Brazilian shares surged to end 5.16 percent higher, underpinned by Telebras which soared following remarks by Communications Minister Sergio Motta on the privatization of the telecom sector, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 47 most active stocks ended at 12,523 points. Total market turnover rose to 867.6 million reais ($803.3 million) from Tuesday's close.
Motta on Wednesday reiterated the government's plans to privatize the entire federally-owned Telebras system by the middle of 1998.
He also confirmed that the ministry would issue bid specifications to hire consultants to advise on the sale and break-up of Telebras on October 30.
Brokers said Motta's comments, combined with attractive share prices after four days of losses, prompted investors, particularly banks, to purchase stocks of Telebras and its subsidiaries.
"With little fresh news out, Motta's comments helped pushing investors off the sidelines," a senior trader said.
Some traders said Motta's remarks were the "excuse" players holding long positions needed to push prices higher ahead of the mid-August options and futures index expiries.
Telebras preferred, which accounted for over 50 percent of trade, jumped 7.19 percent, ending at 156.50 reais.
Shares of Telebras' subsidiaries also posted significant gains, helped by several bank reports reiterating buy recommendations on the stocks.
Telemig preferred was the biggest winner among the telecoms stocks, surging 8.11 percent to 200 reais.
Telesp preferred rose 2.63 percent to 350.99 reais, while Telerj preferred gained 3.24 percent to 175 reais.
Other blue-chips also followed the market's upbeat mood.

State oil firm Petrobras preferred rose 2.67 percent to 308 reais on optimism over the future of the company after President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed into law a bill opening the oil sector to private investment.
Private miner CVRD preferred rose 3.2 percent to 29 reais, while state power holding Eletrobras preferred surged 5.96 percent to 622 reais.
Traders said shares could open mixed Thursday as Wednesday's surge could prompt a correction amid continued speculation ahead of the options and futures index settlements.
